content: A valid Secret Santa assignment is a derangement (permutation with no fixed points). The classic naive algorithm - shuffle a list and pair each element with the next, or repeatedly draw names from a hat and restart on a collision - is biased: mathoverflow.net/questions/50049 shows the restart method is not uniform over derangements (P[restart]=5/36 for n=4), and the 'shuffle then pair, retry if anyone self-assigns' approach has quadratic-ish retry behaviour. A random rotation (circular permutation) guarantees a single cycle, no fixed points, and every participant gives and receives exactly once. Rose-Hulman's 'The Secret Santa Problem' (White, 2006) covers derangements with at least one two-cycle. Any re-draw must be deterministic/persisted, never re-run on render.
